5‐FU and 125I interstittal implant followed by precision high‐doses external beam photon therapy is a feasible and effective treatment for unresectable pancreatic cancer and extrahepatica biliary tract cancer.
the combination of 125I implant and PHD external beam therapy with 5‐FU is a feasible approach for patients with adenocarciroma of the pancreas or extrahepatic bile duct.

the development and clinical evaluation of a new treatment modality for the palliation of unresectable adenoma of the pancrea and extrahepatica bile duct.
the development of a novel method of cancer therapy that is based on the use of a new type of high‐energy photon beam (PHD).

this approach is a reasonable option for patients with unresectable pancreas cancer.

the combination of 125I implant and PHD photon therapy is feasible, and the morbidity and survival of patients with pancreas and bile duct cancer treated with 5‐FU is not superior to that of similar patients treated with PHD photon therapy alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of 125I implant with external beam photon therapy ± chemotherapy is feasible, safe, and effective in the palliative treatment of unresectable carcinoma of the pancreas.
125I interstittal implantation, PHD external beam therapy, ± systemic 5‐FU is a safe, well‐tolerated, and effective palliative treatment modality for unresectable pancreatic and bile duct cancers.
125I implant followed by PHD external beam therapy and 5FU is feasible and safe, but the results are not superior to those of other modalities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
125I interstial implant is a morbid treatment and does not appear to offer a survival advantage over other treatment options.
125I implant followed by PHD external beam therapy is a morbid procedure that does not seem to provide superior patient survival to that of PHD external beam radiation therapy ± 5‐FU.
